title: UM NL Global Studies Scholarship
program_type: University scholarship awarded on separate competitive application, restricted to one named bachelor's programme (Global Studies)
funding_type: Full tuition waiver + living allowance + insurance/visa/training at cost (university-funded)
implementing_agency: UM International Services Desk (payments, insurance, visa costs, Pre-Academic Training), with the UM Scholarship Office, the Global Studies admission office and the Global Studies Scholarship selection committee
programme_action: UM NL Scholarship programme — Global Studies (bachelor's) variant
description: The UM NL Global Studies Scholarship offers one full-coverage scholarship per academic year for the bachelor's programme in Global Studies at Maastricht University, comprising a tuition-fee waiver, a monthly living stipend, health and liability insurance, visa application costs, Pre-Academic Training costs and the first block of the International Student Ambassador Programme, all at cost and arranged by the UM International Services Desk. It is open to incoming bachelor students with demonstrable financial need who hold the nationality of an OECD Official Development Assistance-eligible country (Surinam excluded), have no EU/EEA, Swiss or Surinamese dual nationality, and have been (conditionally) admitted to Global Studies. The award runs for the full 36 months of the programme and includes a mandatory two-week UM Pre-Academic Training. Applicants must first complete the Global Studies admission application by 10 December 2026 and then submit the scholarship application by 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET.

award_types: Full-coverage scholarship for the 36-month bachelor's programme in Global Studies
programme_structure.award_types_detail: One full-coverage scholarship per academic year, covering tuition fees at cost per academic year, a living-expenses allowance of EUR 20,150 per academic year, health and liability insurance at cost, visa application costs at cost, Pre-Academic Training costs at cost, and the International Student Ambassador Programme (ISAP) at cost for the first block only.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Awarded once for the whole 36-month programme rather than renewed annually. The published living-expenses figure is expressly subject to change for academic year 2028-2029, and continued payment depends on the conditions set out in the award letter.

status_note: Applications for the 2027-2028 academic year are open from 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET, so the cycle is currently open as of 2026-10-03. The Global Studies admission application file must be complete by 10 December 2026, and the online UM scholarship portal is stated to be unavailable between 22 and 26 October 2026 due to an upgrade. Next expected cycle after this one: applications for academic year 2028-2029 are expected to open on 1 October 2027.
verification_notes: Confirmed directly on the official Maastricht University scholarship page for the UM NL Global Studies Scholarship, plus the Global Studies programme, admission-requirements, tuition-fees, handling-fee, Pre-Academic Training and UM scholarship-overview pages on maastrichtuniversity.nl. Eleven official-domain pages were fetched. Amount, duration, eligibility, deadline and selection steps are quoted from the official source. Items not published by UM and therefore left null or marked unverified: exact euro amount of the tuition/insurance/visa components (all quoted 'at cost'), the tuition-fee tier that applies to Global Studies, minimum English test scores, and a verified programme photograph.
source_last_updated: 2027-2028 cycle (scholarship page carries 2027-2028 amounts and 2027 dates)

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Applications open 1 October and close 1 February at 23:59 CET
application_deadline.application_period: 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) for academic year 2027-2028
application_deadline.official_rule: Applications are open from 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET. Separately, the applicant must have applied for admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme at UM for the 2027-2028 academic year and submitted the application file in full, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026; by the 1 February 2027 scholarship deadline all registration requirements must be met except legal residence, tuition payment and a hard copy of the diploma.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Two distinct deadlines apply. The Global Studies admission application file must be complete before 10 December 2026, and the scholarship application form must be submitted by 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET. Missing the 10 December admission deadline makes the applicant ineligible even if the scholarship form is submitted on time. The scholarship portal is stated to be unavailable between 22 and 26 October 2026.

programme_duration.renewal_note: The scholarship is granted once for the full 36-month bachelor's programme in Global Studies. The living-expenses amount of EUR 20,150 per academic year is subject to change for academic year 2028-2029.

funding.scholarship_type: Full-coverage scholarship: tuition-fee waiver plus living allowance, with insurance, visa, training and ISAP costs covered at cost
funding.monthly_amount_note: EUR 1,550 per month, included within the EUR 20,150 living-expenses allowance per academic year. The official page states the amount is subject to change for academic year 2028-2029.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance or flight funding is published. Air tickets are explicitly not included and must be paid by the candidate; a EUR 100 per month local-travel allowance is included within the living-expenses figure.
funding.institutional_costs: Tuition fees are covered at cost per academic year. Health and liability insurance, visa application costs, Pre-Academic Training costs and the first block of the International Student Ambassador Programme (ISAP) are arranged for and paid at cost by the UM International Services Desk.
funding.fully_funded_note: Tuition fees, a living-expenses allowance of EUR 20,150 per academic year, health and liability insurance, visa application costs, Pre-Academic Training costs and the first block of ISAP are all covered. It is not a complete cost-of-living package: air tickets are excluded and an approximate EUR 75 cleaning fee must be paid to Maastricht Housing upfront. There is no financial or service bond, but accepting the award requires accepting the allocated room until 16 July 2028 and agreeing to act as a Global Studies and UM ambassador.

tuition.conditions: At cost per academic year, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk; subject to change for academic year 2028-2029. No euro amount is published on the scholarship page. UM's tuition-fee page lists 2027/28 institutional rates for non-EU/EEA full-time bachelor students of EUR 13,400 (low), EUR 18,700 (high) and EUR 32,000 (top); the scholarship page does not state which tier applies to Global Studies, though Global Studies is expressly exempt from the BKKI small-scale-and-intensive surcharge that applies to the UCM and MSP bachelor's programmes.

monthly_stipend.conditions: Paid to students by the UM International Services Desk. Subject to change for academic year 2028-2029. Monthly breakdown: housing EUR 960, groceries and personal hygiene EUR 160, telephone EUR 60, travel EUR 100, books and study materials EUR 90, clothing/hobbies/going out EUR 125, miscellaneous EUR 55.

travel_allowance.note: No travel allowance is provided. Air tickets are explicitly not included and must be paid by the candidate.

visa_support.conditions: Visa application costs at cost, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk.

insurance.conditions: Health and liability insurance at cost, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk.

book_allowance.note: No separate book allowance. EUR 90 per month for books and study materials is included within the EUR 1,550 monthly living-allowance figure.

family_allowance.note: Not published in official source. The mandatory allocated accommodation is not suitable for partners/spouses, children or pets.

accommodation_support.conditions: A room is allocated to scholarship holders until 16 July 2028. Accepting the scholarship means accepting the room, and refusing the room means the scholarship is cancelled. The accommodation is not suitable for partners/spouses, children or pets. Students must find housing for the second and third year themselves. A cleaning fee of approximately EUR 75 is not included and must be paid to Maastricht Housing upfront.

bond.note: No financial or service bond is published. Recipients agree to become an active Global Studies and UM ambassador during and after their studies, committing to share their experiences during at least one (information) session for students and/or other stakeholders.

total_estimated_value.note: Not published as a single total. The tuition, insurance, visa and Pre-Academic Training components are quoted 'at cost' rather than as fixed amounts, so no official total award value exists and none is computed here.

The scholarship is aimed at nationals who require a Dutch entry visa (MVV) and residence permit, and eligibility requires meeting the requirements for obtaining them; the scholarship neither grants nor guarantees a residence permit, and UM can only formally apply for a residence permit once all admission and enrolment requirements are met.

final_year_condition: Applicants in their final year of secondary/high school are eligible: UM requires only conditional admission to Global Studies by the scholarship deadline, and the scholarship rules exempt a hard copy of the diploma from the registration requirements due by 1 February 2027 (the certified diploma copy is an enrolment task due 31 August 2027). A non-Dutch diploma equivalent to the Dutch VWO qualifies for admission; UM publishes a list of VWO-equivalent diplomas and evaluates others individually.
equivalent_degree_note: A non-Dutch diploma equivalent to the Dutch VWO qualifies in principle for admission to Global Studies, and UM assesses non-listed diplomas individually; applicants without the required diploma may be admitted via the Colloquium Doctum entrance examination. However, for the scholarship a diploma from a higher education institution or a completed degree programme equivalent to a bachelor's makes the applicant ineligible.
nationality_quota: Non-EU/EEA only (OECD ODA-eligible nationalities, Surinam excluded, no EU/EEA, Swiss or Surinamese dual nationality). One full-coverage award per academic year for the Global Studies programme; the selection committee interviews a top-5 and keeps a reserve list.

eligibility.citizenship: Nationality of a country eligible to receive Official Development Assistance from the OECD, with Surinam excluded; no dual nationality from an EU/EEA country, Switzerland or Surinam.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must meet the requirements for obtaining an entry visa (MVV) and residence permit for the Netherlands. Applicants who already hold a residence permit for another Schengen country may apply only if it remains valid until at least 2 September 2027; if it expires before that date the application must be made from the home country via an MVV visa application.
eligibility.age_limit: Maximum age 35 on 1 September 2027. No minimum age is published.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: A Dutch VWO diploma, an HBO or OU propaedeutic diploma, or a non-Dutch diploma equivalent to the Dutch VWO. Applicants who do not hold the required diploma may be eligible via the Colloquium Doctum entrance examination.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Conditional admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme with the complete admission application file submitted before 10 December 2026. Global Studies is a selective programme: the Board of Admissions scores applications against published criteria and applications must receive a minimum score to be selected.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Continuous good to excellent results during prior education, with the latest grade transcript showing at least 75% of the maximum grade. The official example given is 3 out of 4, equivalent to 7.5 out of 10 at Maastricht University.
eligibility.language_requirement: English is the language of instruction. Applicants answer UM's online language-requirements questionnaire on the Global Studies admission-requirements page to determine whether additional proof of English proficiency is required; the outcome indicates which documents can be used to prove proficiency. No minimum IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo score is published on the pages read.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required. (Job) experience may be described in the curriculum vitae.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Yes. The curriculum vitae must document proven previous extracurricular engagement with a previous (academic) organisation or high school and active citizenship in the applicant's community, plus any awards or prizes.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not stated as a separate requirement. Personal development potential, active citizenship and a commitment to act as a Global Studies and UM ambassador are assessed.
eligibility.financial_need: Yes. Demonstrable financial need is part of the stated target group, and a personal statement of financial needs describing personal circumstances (financial difficulty, sole parent/caretaking responsibilities, medical condition, disability, refugee status and so on) is a required document.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Only one UM scholarship may be applied for; multiple scholarship applications are disqualified. Only one application may be submitted for this scholarship and documents cannot be added or replaced after submission.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be an incoming (first-year) bachelor student who has not obtained a diploma from a higher education institution and has not completed a degree programme equivalent to a bachelor's.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health requirement is published. Health and liability insurance is arranged for and paid at cost by the UM International Services Desk.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Global Studies bachelor's programme only, offered within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences (FASoS).

academic_requirements.percentage_note: The latest grade transcript must show at least 75% of the maximum grade. The official example given is 3 out of 4, equivalent to 7.5 out of 10 at Maastricht University.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Conditional admission to the Global Studies bachelor's programme with the complete admission file submitted before 10 December 2026. Global Studies is selective, requiring a minimum Board of Admissions score, a motivation statement in English (template in the MyApplication portal, 7 questions, maximum 250 words each) and an essay question form in English (template, maximum 300 words). Applicants may also be asked for a portrait picture, passport or EU/EEA identity card copy, and grades transcript.
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: UM states that scholarship applicants are assessed on academic excellence, extracurricular engagement, active citizenship and financial need, and that because the number of scholarships is limited the selection process is highly competitive. No numerical weighting is published.

english_requirement.moi_rule: UM determines the required proof of English proficiency through an online language-requirements questionnaire on the Global Studies admission-requirements page; the outcome indicates which documents can be used to prove proficiency. No medium-of-instruction (MOI) waiver rule is published on the pages read.
english_requirement.test_score_note: No minimum IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo score is published on the Global Studies admission-requirements page or any other UM page fetched. Proof of English proficiency is required 'if applicable' as determined by the programme's language-requirements questionnaire.

language_of_instruction.language_note: Global Studies is taught entirely in English. The admission motivation statement and the essay question form must be written in English. Dutch is not required for admission.

application_method.application_route: Two-step route: first apply for the Global Studies bachelor's programme via Studielink.nl to obtain a UM student ID number, then log in with the UM account and complete the online UM scholarship application form, uploading all documents in a single submission.
application_steps: Step 1: Apply for the Global Studies bachelor's programme at Maastricht University via Studielink and obtain a UM student ID number. The complete admission application file must be submitted, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026.

Step 2: Log in with the UM account and fill in the online scholarship application form, uploading the curriculum vitae, motivation letter, proof of academic excellence, personal statement of financial needs, reference letter and referee contact details in .doc, .docx or PDF format, and submit once only.
Selection step 1: The UM International Services Desk checks whether all applications are complete after 1 February 2027.
Selection step 2: The UM Scholarship Office forwards the application to the Global Studies admission office.

Selection step 3: The Global Studies admission office, with the programme coordinator(s), ranks the application against the UM scholarship selection criteria and proposes a top-5 to the Global Studies Scholarship selection committee in March 2027.

Selection step 4: The Global Studies Scholarship selection committee (the Global Studies academic programme coordinator plus UM Scholarship Office representatives) invites the top-5 applicants to an online interview and takes a decision; unselected applicants are added to a reserve list.

Selection step 5: The UM International Services Desk informs all candidates of their status in April 2027; status becomes selected, waitlisted or rejected by the beginning of June 2027 at the latest, and waitlisted statuses are resolved by June 2027.

Step 6: Sign and return the award letter to the UM International Services Desk to accept the scholarship. Awardees then receive information about the UM Pre-Academic Training programme and arrival in Maastricht.
application_method.application_fee: A programme handling fee of EUR 100 excluding bank costs applies to applicants whose diploma is based on a non-EU/EEA curriculum. This fee is NOT covered by the scholarship, must be received by Maastricht University by 10 December 2026, and is refunded once the student starts (excluding bank account costs).

selection_process.decision_maker: The Global Studies Scholarship selection committee, composed of the Global Studies academic programme coordinator and representatives of the UM Scholarship Office. The Global Studies admission office, together with the programme coordinator(s), performs the initial ranking; the UM International Services Desk performs the completeness check and informs candidates of the outcome.
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive multi-stage scholarship selection following admission to the Global Studies programme
possible_stages: Completeness check of all applications by the UM International Services Desk after 1 February 2027
Forwarding of the application by the UM Scholarship Office to the Global Studies admission office
Ranking by the Global Studies admission office with the programme coordinator(s) against the UM scholarship selection criteria, and proposal of a top-5 to the selection committee in March 2027
Online interview of the top-5 by the selection committee and decision; unselected applicants are placed on a reserve list
Notification of status (selected, waitlisted or rejected) by the UM International Services Desk in April 2027, resolved by the beginning of June 2027 at the latest

selection_process.official_universal_weighting: UM assesses scholarship applicants on academic excellence, extracurricular engagement, active citizenship and financial need. No percentage weighting is published.
selection_process.weighting_note: No numerical weighting is published. UM states that the number of scholarships is limited and the selection process is highly competitive.
selection_process.results_timing: The UM International Services Desk informs all candidates of their application status in April 2027. Status is selected, waitlisted or rejected by the beginning of June 2027 at the latest, and waitlisted statuses are converted to selected or rejected by June 2027.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: The Global Studies admission office proposes a top-5 to the selection committee in March 2027 and the committee interviews the top-5. Applicants who are not selected are added to a reserve list in case selected candidates decline the scholarship.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Personal development potential; demonstrable engagement and active citizenship documented in the CV; and the applicant's agreement to act as an active Global Studies and UM ambassador during and after their studies, sharing experiences in at least one (information) session. Academic excellence must be shown by a transcript of at least 75% of the maximum grade.

possible_awards: Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Global Studies
degree_outcome.degree_note: Global Studies is a three-year, full-time programme taught by six UM faculties that each contribute equally to the educational content, a structure described by UM as unique in the Netherlands. Students take part in a local or international field study, develop an intervention for a societal problem presented by an NGO, government, agency, firm or school, and write an interdisciplinary bachelor thesis.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Credit transfer or exemptions may be requested after registration for (near-)identical courses passed at a previous research university or university of applied sciences. UM states exemptions are rarely granted because the modules are multi-disciplinary and specific, and that starting in the second year is not an option; students must register as first-year students.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Tuition fees are covered in full at cost per academic year, arranged for and paid by the UM International Services Desk.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The EUR 100 handling fee (excluding bank costs) is NOT covered by the scholarship and must be paid by the applicant by 10 December 2026; it is refunded once the student starts, excluding bank account costs.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients must sign and return the award letter to the UM International Services Desk to accept the scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Access to the UM Student Services, the International Student Helpdesk (ISH), the international buddy programme, UM sports, disability support and the UM Pre-Academic Training programme, whose costs are paid at cost by the UM International Services Desk for scholarship holders.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No financial bond or service bond is published. Recipients accept a mandatory allocated room until 16 July 2028 and agree to become an active Global Studies and UM ambassador during and after their studies, committing to share their experiences during at least one (information) session for students and/or other stakeholders.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Refusing the allocated room results in cancellation of the scholarship.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Use the UM template rather than a free-form letter. Demonstrate motivation for the scholarship specifically, and connect it to the Global Studies programme: show how the interdisciplinary, six-faculty Global Studies curriculum, its local or international field study and its interdisciplinary bachelor thesis uniquely support your personal development. Letters are read alongside a CV that must evidence extracurricular engagement and active citizenship in your community, so reference concrete, verifiable commitments rather than general aspirations. State your financial circumstances honestly and specifically in the separate financial-needs statement. Keep the CV to two A4 pages and lead with academic results because the transcript must show at least 75% of the maximum grade. Applicants are encouraged to write responses themselves rather than relying on AI tools, since generic AI-generated answers make applications harder to assess.

Applying with an existing Schengen residence permit that expires before 2 September 2027 instead of applying from the home country via MVV

risk_flags.risk: Two-stage deadline trap: the Global Studies admission file must be complete before 10 December 2026, roughly two months before the 1 February 2027 scholarship deadline.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who submits the scholarship form on time but whose admission file was incomplete before 10 December is ineligible regardless of application quality.
risk_flags.mitigation: Register on Studielink immediately when applications open on 1 October 2026, pay the handling fee early, and complete all admission tasks well before 10 December 2026.

risk_flags.risk: Single-submission rule: the scholarship application can be submitted only once, and documents cannot be added or replaced.
risk_flags.impact: Any missing or non-compliant document (CV, motivation letter, transcript, financial-needs statement, reference letter, referee details) makes the application incomplete and disqualifies it.
risk_flags.mitigation: Assemble and check every document, including the reference letter and full referee contact details, before opening the submission form.

risk_flags.risk: Only one award per academic year for this programme, with a top-5 interview shortlist and a reserve list.
risk_flags.impact: A qualified applicant may be ranked well but not selected; unselected applicants are waitlisted until June 2027 at the latest.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply for other UM-external or national funding in parallel, while noting that only one UM scholarship may be applied for.

risk_flags.risk: Residence-permit dependency: eligibility requires meeting the requirements for a Dutch entry visa (MVV) and residence permit, and holders of a Schengen residence permit must have it valid until at least 2 September 2027.
risk_flags.impact: The award is designed for applicants who require a Dutch residence permit; the scholarship neither grants nor guarantees one, and UM can only apply to the IND once all admission and enrolment requirements are met.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the country in which the MVV must be collected before applying, keep passport and permit expiry dates in view, and complete admission and enrolment tasks early enough for UM to file with the IND before 1 July for a September start.

risk_flags.risk: Costs are quoted 'at cost' for tuition, insurance, visa and Pre-Academic Training, with no published euro amounts.
risk_flags.impact: The total value of the award cannot be calculated, and the published EUR 20,150 living allowance is subject to change for academic year 2028-2029, so years two and three are not cost-certain.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget against UM's published 2027/28 institutional tuition-fee rates and treat only the living-expense figure for the first academic year as firm.

risk_flags.risk: Mandatory allocated accommodation until 16 July 2028, with refusal causing cancellation of the scholarship, and no room for partners, spouses, children or pets.
risk_flags.impact: Family applicants and applicants with specific housing requirements may be unable to accept the award; housing for years two and three is self-funded.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm willingness to accept the allocated room before applying, note that religious and similar preferences are taken into account, and plan independently for years two and three.

risk_flags.risk: Security and continuity obligations: a mandatory two-week UM Pre-Academic Training in the first week of August 2027, plus active ambassador duties during and after the studies.
risk_flags.impact: Missing the Pre-Academic Training or refusing the ambassador commitment puts the award at risk; the training falls immediately before the September 2027 start.
risk_flags.mitigation: Keep August 2027 free after award notification in April 2027 and confirm attendance in the award letter.

risk_flags.risk: Portal and process disruption: UM states the scholarship portal is unavailable between 22 and 26 October 2026 due to an upgrade.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants attempting to submit during that window cannot do so and may lose time before the 10 December admission deadline.
risk_flags.mitigation: Prepare all documents early and submit outside the 22-26 October 2026 portal outage window.

database_notes: Official award name is 'UM NL Global Studies Scholarship'. The task brief called it 'Maastricht University Global Studies Scholarship', but no such name appears on the official page; legacy_titles is therefore empty rather than populated with the requester's paraphrase.

No substitution was made: the assigned target is a live bachelor's-level scholarship in the Netherlands (an allowed region), is not on the do-not-duplicate list in RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md, and is not covered by the exclusion scope. The record was written to the assigned filename 12-netherlands-maastricht-global-studies.json.

The award is a university scholarship of the UM 'NL' family (which also includes the UM NL-High Potential, UM NL Brightlands Talent and UM NL Social Justice scholarships). It is NOT confirmed to be the Dutch Ministry of Education-funded Holland Scholarship linked from the page; that is a separate EUR 5,000 one-off grant. admin_authority is therefore recorded as Maastricht University itself.

The page contains an internal tension on the number of awards: 'one full coverage scholarship (including a tuition fee waiver and monthly stipend) per academic year' alongside 'for a selected number of top-performing bachelor students', and a top-5 interview shortlist with a reserve list. The selection procedure indicates a single selection from a top-5. This is flagged in verification.programme_check_required.

The official page states the Pre-Academic Training is 'a two week mandatory component' and also that it 'takes place in the first week of August 2027'. Both statements are recorded as published; the 2026 edition of the PAT programme ran 3-14 August 2026, which is consistent with two weeks starting in the first week of August.

Cost items the scholarship does not cover the scholarship does not cover: air tickets, an approximate EUR 75 cleaning fee payable to Maastricht Housing upfront, housing beyond 16 July 2028, and the EUR 100 programme handling fee.

bachelor_requirement is false in the sense that no completed bachelor's degree is required; in fact holding a higher-education diploma or a bachelor-equivalent degree disqualifies an applicant from this scholarship.

Health and liability insurance is covered 'at cost' with no published euro amount; the sibling UM NL-High Potential Scholarship page quotes EUR 700 for insurance, but that figure is not stated for the Global Studies award and was deliberately not carried over.

The tuition-fee page confirms Global Studies is exempt from the BKKI small-scale-and-intensive surcharge that applies to the UCM and MSP bachelor's programmes, but does not state which of the three institutional tiers (low/high/top) Global Studies falls into, so no tuition amount is asserted.
